definitions: Alan Mathison Turing (1912–1954), an English mathematician and logician, widely considered to be the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence.
A machine, later called a universal Turing machine, conceived by Alan Turing in 1936, which can simulate any algorithm.
examples: Turing's work laid the foundation for modern computing.
The Turing test is a measure of a machine's ability to exhibit intelligent behaviour equivalent to, or indistinguishable from, that of a human.
